method: Built-in image generation, followed by export to 100x88 pixels with a 96-colour palette and transparent alpha.

assets.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Repaint the FIRST input icon as actual detailed HIGH-COLOUR PIXEL ART for a Hearts of Iron IV focus button. The SECOND input is the original DLC icon at game resolution, giving the approximate detail density, colour depth and compact icon proportions.
Keep exactly the first image's single red Fokker Dr.I triplane with THREE connected wings, two landing wheels and a propeller; dark blue pointed shield and silver aviation wings. Preserve its composition, object count, frame, principal colours, pose and silhouette. Change only the rendering into MORE DISTINCT PIXEL ART than before.
Imagine a 100 x 88 pixel native sprite, then show a clean integer enlarged version of that sprite: coherent crisp pixel clusters, visibly stepped contours, grouped 1-3 pixel highlights, compact dark outlines, limited 3-5 tone shading per material and a restricted high-colour palette of roughly 64-96 colours. This should read as a professionally hand-pixelled strategy-game badge, with enough material shading to belong beside the DLC reference. Eliminate realistic scratches, pores, cloth fibres, smooth glossy gradients, painterly smearing and tiny independent rivets; simplify them into intentional pixel marks.
No photorealistic or 3D rendering. No vector art. No huge low-detail 8-bit blocks. No smoothing of the pixel clusters. No dotted overlay, artificial grid lines or checkerboard pattern drawn onto the image. Do not add letters, numerals, logos, captions, extra emblems or glowing effects. Preserve genuine transparent background. Final composition ratio 100:88 with small transparent margins; keep every part inside the canvas.
